title: Chronological usage bridge and cost anchoring worker
creator: Emily Chen
description: Build a streaming + epochal bridge worker that deterministically anchors sub-second usage events into billable windows and produces tidy cost records for downstream billing. The job must handle out-of-order/late events, idempotent writes, and be resilient to partition rebalances. This is intended to replace several fragile ad-hoc backfills and reduce late-arrival charge corrections.
background: Current billing pipeline ingests many small events from the serving layer (streamed token-attribution records, session heartbeats, model-route decisions). These are stored as raw events and later compacted into billing rows via multiple ad-hoc jobs. We see recurring issues: late arrivals causing retro credits, high read amplification in the nightly compactor, and difficult-to-debug inconsistencies between real-time usage and invoice drafts. During the Sep incident (INC-2025-09-14) a spike in out-of-order session joins caused ~1.8% of customers to see provisional credits which required manual reconciliation.
acceptance_criteria: A streaming worker consumes raw usage topic and emits per-customer, per-window cost records with deterministic keys (customer_id|window_ts|route|model_variant)
Late arrivals within the 4-hour correction window are merged into existing window rows without producing duplicate billed tokens
Writes to the billing sink are idempotent; replaying the same input interval produces no net change
End-to-end latency: 50th percentile < 30s, 95th percentile < 5m for normal load
Includes health metrics and dashboards: processing lag, reprocessing queue depth, tombstone rate, idempotency conflicts
Automated integration test that replays synthetic out-of-order events and validates final windowed totals against a golden reference
design_notes: Use Kafka compacted topics for the canonical windowed ledger (keyed by customer-window-route); worker will materialize state in RocksDB (Kafka Streams) to support local merges and checkpointing
Compaction + tombstone technique used to mark finalized windows older than correction window to allow cheaper cold storage compaction
Expose a deterministic conflict-resolution rule: latest event wins by ingest_ts, except when event has the explicit "force_annotate" flag from downstream audits
Considerations: Postgres would simplify ad-hoc queries but does not scale well for high-cardinality customer-window rows; RocksDB allows per-partition state with efficient local merges
Security: billing sink writes must be signed and audited; integrate with existing KMS token used by billing writer service
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Prototype Kafka Streams job (local dev) that consumes raw-usage.v1 and writes to billing-window.compacted.v1
Phase 2: Add idempotent write layer to billing sink (pre-write compare+merge using compacted topic snapshot), add metrics
Phase 3: Canary in eu-west-1 with 5 pilot customers, monitor metrics and run parity checks vs nightly compactor
Phase 4: Roll forward across regions and turn off nightly compactor after two weeks of parity and manual audits
test_plan: Unit tests for deterministic keying and merge logic
Integration test harness that replays recorded live traffic including out-of-order sequences from Aug replay dump
Load test: sustained 2x peak QPS for 6 hours against canary cluster, validate consumer lag and RocksDB memory usage
End-to-end regression tests that compare canary outputs to historical invoice data for selected tenants
rollout_plan: Deploy prototype to staging, run 48h smoke and parity checks
Canary with 5 low-risk pilot tenants in eu-west-1 for 72h
Expand to 25% of traffic and run automated parity vs legacy compactor for 7 days
If all parity checks pass, promote to 100% and decommission nightly compactor with a 30-day rollback window
